grade: C- (correct directional bias overridden by excessive caution; sizing/conviction mismatch)
observations: <parameter name="provisional_lessons">["When aggressive call and conservative call diverge sharply (stand_aside vs 0.55 short) and price is chopping near a wall (7448-7450 tagged almost exactly per the 15:00 aggressive read), the market often needs one more failed test before it breaks — the read was right, timing/patience was the gap, not direction.", "At 14:30 the aggressive short thesis was flat-out wrong (market ripped +53 to 7450 instead of breaking down) — this is a reminder that 'no support below' reasoning near a wall can fail badly if the wall itself gets broken upward first; walls can flip from resistance to launchpad.", "Once the top was actually tagged (7450) at 14:45/15:00, the subsequent moves were huge clean breakdowns (-60, -107, -79 pts) that were flagged correctly in direction and even in the specific target zones (7405-7395, 7395), but conservative stand_aside missed nearly the entire move — being 0.3 conviction stand_aside three cycles in a row while aggressive kept calling the same fade-short thesis and kept being validated is a pattern worth watching: repeated aggressive conviction that later proves right should probably start upgrading the conservative stance sooner.", "The 15:10 'short (0.4)' call finally aligned conservative with the actual move, but by then most of the 100+pt drop was already captured only by the aggressive line, not by the more cautious default — suggests conservative threshold may be miscalibrated to react only after confirmation that costs most of the move.", "One session is not enough to conclude 'always trust aggressive over conservative near identified walls' — this could easily be a case of a lucky sequential read on a trending gamma unwind day; need more days with mixed/choppy outcomes to see if aggressive calls get punished as often as they get rewarded."]

Overall regime: strong persistent uptrend all day, spot ~7668 (10:30) to session highs ~7758 (15:46) before a sharp late fade to 7736.5 close. Every dip was bought; no meaningful reversal materialized until the final 20 minutes.

Conservative model stood aside for ~95% of the day (0.55-0.85 confidence stand_aside), missing the entire ~90pt uptrend from 7668→7758. Only flipped to 'long'/'short' briefly at 11:25 (long, correctly, after price already up ~34pts) and again 14:43-14:44 (short, which was WRONG — price rallied from 7740 to 7755 after that short call, a real miss/loss setup).

Aggressive model was long almost continuously from 10:38/10:40 (@7675.63) through repeated hold/trail instructions, riding the move from 7675 to peak entries around 7750-7755 — this was the single best decision of the day, capturing the bulk of the ~80pt trend.

Aggressive round-tripped through several re-entries (7675.63 -> implied exits/re-adds at 7689.79 (11:08), 7703.91 (11:39), 7709.49 (11:56), 7718.03 (12:32), 7745.91 (14:53), 7750.91 (15:01), 7755.17 (15:20)) — each new entry chased a higher king_node/wall level as price kept breaking through. This trend-following re-entry cadence worked well on the way up.

Around 13:30-13:38 aggressive flipped to a SHORT scalp at 7734.69 targeting 7725, explicitly countertrend against the day's dominant uptrend. Price never came close to 7725 — it continued higher to 7745+ over the next 45m (max_down only -1.3, max_up +17). This countertrend short was a clear LOSER, and the model's own notes for later re-entries (14:40-14:49 short from 7740.37 targeting 7726) also failed to hit target; price only dipped modestly before resuming to make new highs (7755+) — another countertrend short that underperformed vs simply staying long/flat.
14:50 aggressive explicitly exited the short 'thesis invalidated' — good adaptive discipline, avoided compounding the countertrend loss.

Late day (15:09 onward): after price tagged 7755 king node and pushed to session high 7758 at 15:46, it reversed HARD, dropping from 7758 to 7736.5 by the 15:55-16:00 close (a ~21pt round-trip down). Any long entered in the 15:01-15:46 window (7750.91, 7755.17, 7756.5, 7758 chase) would have been sitting on open losses at the close (max_down readings of -16 to -21.5 in the final entries) — the last few 'long' aggressive calls (15:45, 15:46 chasing 7756.5/7758) were poorly timed, buying right at the top of the range into the eventual reversal.

The wall/king-node framework (7700, 7715/7725, 7740, 7755, 7770) correctly identified sequential resistance levels that price paused at before breaking through each time on the way up — useful map, though the model was consistently too conservative on trim targets (e.g., repeatedly capping targets at 7695/7698/7699 under the 7700 wall) versus letting the position run, which would have captured much more (spot eventually reached 7758, ~60pts beyond the first 7698 cap).

15:55 EOD-flatten mentality (conservative/aggressive both stand_aside heavy by 15:50-16:00) avoided being long into the final reversal — this effectively saved money since the 15:46-15:47 chase-long entries were the ones caught by the reversal; the model had NOT added new size in the last 10 minutes, which was protective.
